sources.location: RAW headers read by HTTP range request (instrument, method file, activation type; scratchpad/PXD012332/evidence/raw_header_check.json)

claims.value: glucose (reactors A, B, E) or xylose (reactors A, C, F) × early exponential / late exponential / lipid production phase
claims.evidence: RAW names <date>_SLU_<reactor><n><G|X>: G/X = glucose/xylose, letter = bioreactor (three per carbon source, 'cultivations … performed in triplicate'), n = sampling point; glucose n = 1, 2, 8 and xylose n = 2, 5, 10 are ordered as the three proteome sampling phases t1–t3 of paper Fig 1
Table 1: 'batch cultivation of R. toruloides CBS 14'

claims.value: Q Exactive; HCD 28 NCE; top-12 DDA
claims.evidence: Methods: 'Q-Exactive … (Top12 method) … NCE setting of 28'; RAW headers: Q Exactive, 120min_top12 method

claims.value: CAM C fixed; Acetyl protein N-term, Ox M, Deamidated N/Q variable; 4.5 ppm / 20 ppm; trypsin
claims.evidence: Methods: MaxQuant 1.5.3.40, 4.5 ppm MS / 20 ppm MS/MS, Trypsin/P, fixed carbamidomethylation, variable protein N-terminal acetylation, Met oxidation, N/Q deamidation

limitations: The growth phase is inferred from the order of the sampling-point token in the file names; the paper gives 8/16/64 h (glucose) and 16/40/96 h (xylose). Glucose tokens 1/2/8 match 8-h sampling intervals, but the xylose lipid-phase token 10 would mean 80 h rather than 96 h, so no sampling time in hours is annotated.
The same reactor letter 'A' is used for one glucose and one xylose cultivation; they are different bioreactor runs.
Trypsin/P in the search is annotated as Trypsin. The lysis buffer contained DTT (paper Methods); the alkylation reagent is not stated, and no reagent columns are annotated.
